scaffolding: Pure-Python stub of torch, with only what the snippet touches: _Tensor (to, argmax, view_as, eq, sum, item), _Model (train, call), _Loss (item, backward), _Optimizer (zero_grad, step) and DataLoader (iteration, len, dataset).
Namespaces torch, nn and optim with device, Module, modules and Optimizer: the annotations in the signature of train are evaluated when the function is defined, so the names must exist.

The stub does real training, in miniature: the model is one bias per class added to the score of the sample; the loss is the mean of how much the highest score exceeds that of the correct class; backward accumulates the gradient of the bias, zero_grad resets it, step applies it with rate 0.5. So the result depends on zero_grad, backward and step being called correctly in each batch, and the tests check the effect of training instead of the order of the calls.
run(batches): builds the model, the optimizer and the loader of the stub, calls train and returns (loss, accuracy, final bias, whether the model is in training mode).
Checked: Pysmell only flags train (PAR=5); nothing in the scaffolding.
pinned_behavior: typical: two batches with hits and misses; loss 0.28125, accuracy 50.0, final bias [0.25, -0.25, 0], model in training mode. Whether the 1st sample of batch 2 is a hit depends on the step of batch 1; the final bias depends on the gradient being reset between batches. Also pins the peculiarity of the original: it sums the mean losses of the batches and divides by the number of samples.
edge: a single batch, all correct; loss 0, accuracy 100.0, bias unchanged, model in training mode.
invalid: an empty dataset raises ZeroDivisionError (line 160 of the original).
not_pinned_on_purpose: Description of the tqdm progress bar (stderr): cosmetic and mixed with elapsed time.
.to(device): has no observable effect in the stub.
Identity of the returned model: the test checks the final state (bias, training mode), not whether it is the same object.
